intro: The present continuous (be + verb-ing) describes what is happening now, or around now for a short time. Many languages use one present tense for this; English uses a different form, and this lesson shows you when.
objectifs: Make the present continuous: am / is / are + verb-ing, in all forms.
Use the spelling rules for -ing (making, running, lying).
Use the present continuous for actions happening now, temporary situations and changes.
Know the signal words: now, at the moment, today, this week, Look!, Listen!

texte: Make the present continuous with “to be” in the present (am, is, are) + the verb with -ing. All the rules of “to be” from lessons 1 and 4 work here: short forms, negatives with not, questions with a change of order, short answers with be.
The -ing verb never changes with the subject: only “be” changes.

lignes: I'm working. / She's working. / They're working.
I'm not working. / He isn't working. / We aren't working.
Are you working? / Is she working?
Yes, I am. / No, she isn't.
What are you doing? / Where is he going?

exemples: What are you reading? — A novel.

texte: Most verbs just add -ing. Three rules change the spelling.

Double the last letter in one-syllable verbs that end in consonant + vowel + consonant (run, sit, stop), and in two-syllable verbs stressed on the last syllable (beGIN → beginning). Don't double w, x or y: snow → snowing, fix → fixing, play → playing.

lignes: work → working, eat → eating, play → playing, study → studying
silent e at the end: remove it
make → making, write → writing, come → coming, dance → dancing
run → running, sit → sitting, swim → swimming, stop → stopping, begin → beginning
lie → lying, die → dying, tie → tying

sections.note: British / American: travel → travelling (UK) / traveling (US). British English doubles a final l even when the stress is not on the last syllable.

texte: The first use is an action happening at the moment of speaking. Here the present continuous is necessary: “I eat” is wrong for this moment.
Signal words: now, right now, at the moment, at present. “Look!” and “Listen!” show an action that is happening.
exemples: Sorry, I can't talk. I'm driving.
Listen! Someone is knocking at the door.
The children are sleeping right now.

sections.titre: Use 2: a temporary situation around now
texte: The present continuous also describes an activity that continues for some time around now, even if you are not doing it at this second. The idea is “in this period of my life, for a limited time”.
Signal words: today, this week, this month, this year, these days, currently.
Compare: “I live in Lyon” (present simple: my permanent situation) / “I'm living in Lyon this year” (present continuous: temporary).
exemples: I'm reading a very good book this week.

texte: Use the present continuous for a situation that is slowly changing, often with verbs like get (become), become, change, grow, increase, improve.
This tense can also talk about future plans that are already arranged (I'm meeting Paul tomorrow). You will study this use in lesson 50. For now, just know that it exists.

Some verbs describe a state, not an action: like, love, hate, want, need, know, understand, believe, remember, own, belong. Use them in the present simple, even for now: I want a coffee now (not “I'm wanting”). Lesson 9 explains this and compares the two present tenses.
“Have” for possession follows the same rule (I have a car), but “have” for an action can take -ing: I'm having lunch.
exemples: I don't understand. ✓ / I'm not understanding. ✗

formule: subject + am / is / are (+ not) + verb-ing · Am / Is / Are + subject + verb-ing?
prononciation: -ing is /ɪŋ/: a short i and a nasal sound at the back of the mouth, with no hard g at the end.
In informal speech you often hear /ɪn/ (“workin'”): understand it, but don't write it.
Short forms join the subject: I'm /aɪm/, she's /ʃiːz/, they're /ðeə/. In the sentence, stress the -ing verb: I'm WORking.
In “What are you doing?”, “are” is weak: /wɒt ə jə ˈduːɪŋ/. Informally it can sound like “Whatcha doing?”.
Doubled verbs keep a short sound: running /ˈrʌnɪŋ/ (short u). Compare writing /ˈraɪtɪŋ/ (long i).
erreurs: Consonant + vowel + consonant: double the consonant.
“Want” is a state verb: present simple.

dialogue.contexte: On a Saturday afternoon, Malik, in Brussels, calls his sister Inès in Toulouse.
lignes: Hi, Inès! What are you doing?
Hi! I'm sitting in a café with Zoé. We're having a hot chocolate.
Nice! It's raining here. Is it raining in Toulouse?
No, it isn't. The sun is shining. Are you working today?
No, I'm not. I'm painting my new flat this weekend.
Yes, he is, but he's sleeping on the sofa right now!
Ha ha! Typical Sami. Send me a photo!

mots: stay until someone or something comes
when water falls from the sky
turn your eyes to see something
rest on a chair or on the ground
make food hot and ready to eat

exercices.consigne: Put the verb in the present continuous.
items: We ___ (not / watch) TV. You can turn it off.
Look! Those men ___ (run) to the station.
I ___ (study) for an exam this week.

exercices.consigne: Write the question in the present continuous, then the short answer shown.
items: Are you working today? — No, I'm not.
Is it raining in Brussels? — Yes, it is.
Are your parents travelling this month? — Yes, they are.
Is Léo listening? — No, he isn't.

exercices.consigne: Each sentence has one mistake. Correct it.
items: She's cooking dinner now. / She is cooking dinner now.
They are siting in the garden.
They are sitting in the garden.

exercices.consigne: Write one sentence in the present continuous for each situation.
items: You look out of the window. You see snow falling. (Look!)
Your friend asks about your activity now. You have a book in your hands.
What are you doing? — I'm reading.
This week your sister doesn't go to the office. (from home)
She's working from home this week.
The temperature is going up. (get / hot)

exercices.consigne: Write four sentences in the present continuous: what you are doing now, what a person near you is doing, a temporary project this week or month, and a change in progress.
items: I'm sitting at my desk and I'm doing this exercise. My son is playing in the garden. This month I'm learning to drive. It's getting dark outside.

a_retenir: am / is / are + verb-ing. Negative with not; question with be first (never do).
Spelling: making (no e), running (double consonant), lying (-ie → -y).
Uses: action now (now, Look!), temporary situation (this week), change (It's getting cold).
State verbs (want, know, like, understand): present simple, no -ing.
“I eat” = habit; “I'm eating” = now. You must choose.
